newsitem.title: GERMANY: Audi says zeroes in on Brazil plant.
newsitem.headline: Audi says zeroes in on Brazil plant.

text.p: German luxury carmaker Audi AG said on Tuesday that it was "highly probable" that it would decide on Brazil as the site for a new production plant and said a final decision could still be made in 1996.

Brazil has widely been rumoured to be the top site for a new plant to build the compact A3 model for Latin American markets. Audi has only previously said that Brazil was a top candidate but that other areas were under consideration.
The country has been tipped to be the top choice because of potential cost-savings since parent company Volkswagen AG has several facilities in the country.
Audi chief executive Herbert Demel also repeated that sales, production and unit deliveries were all higher and that he expected profits to be clearly above 1995 levels.
He said sales would rise over seven percent for the year when Audi posted 1995 sales of 16.7 billion marks ($11 billion) and a pre-tax profit of 111 million marks.

From January to September, Demel said Audi's sales rose 11.1 percent to 13.6 billion marks compared with 12.3 billion marks in the year-ago period. But Audi's market share in Germany slipped to 5.9 percent from 6.3 percent.

In the first nine months of the year, Demel said Audi produced 355,827 vehicles, up from 328.295 vehicles in the 1995 period, while deliveries to customers rose to 362,274 from 337,938 in the year-ago period.
Sales in Germany rose only slightly to 159,498 vehicles compared with 158,208 vehicles in the 1995 period.
The carmaker also said its investments had risen sharply to 981 million marks compared with 508 million marks, while its workfroce rose by almost 2,000 to 35,362 workers.
